findings.title: Visible-seconds E204 clock breaks the existing fake-clock e2e case
findings.section: Task 14 — The music-font clock, and AlphaTab's own error event (Step 3, player.e2e.ts)
findings.why_it_matters: If the implementer follows Task 14 as written, the web e2e lane goes red. The existing case 'a music font that arrives after the 60 s backstop clears the error' (web/e2e/player.e2e.ts:230) reaches E204 by retrying `page.clock.fastForward(61_000)` inside a 20-second `toPass`. In Playwright 1.61.1, fastForward fires each due timer at most once: `_innerFastForwardTo` moves every timer's callAt to the target, then `_runTo` runs it once. So each retry adds one tick to the new one-second counter, which needs 60. The plan says this case passes unchanged because the page is always visible, which points the implementer at the clock design (choice 7, the one-second counter) instead of the test. Switching the case to `runFor`, which fires every interval tick, keeps both the design and what the case proves.
findings.suggested_fix: Add web/e2e/player.e2e.ts:230 to Task 14's Files and Step 3. In 'a music font that arrives after the 60 s backstop clears the error', replace `await page.clock.fastForward(61_000);` with `await page.clock.runFor(61_000);`. Reword the comment above it: fastForward fires a due timer at most once, while runFor fires every one-second tick of the visible-time clock. Keep the toPass retry.
evidence: Expected: PASS — including the existing 60-second backstop case, which headless Chromium runs in a page that is always visible.
The E204 clock is a one-second counter

findings.title: report.test.ts cases see earlier cases' stand-in Sentry calls
findings.section: Task 5 — The reporting functions, report.ts (Step 2, report.test.ts)
findings.why_it_matters: About nine of the 22 cases in Task 5's own test file fail, and so does the E105 case Task 11 adds. In Vitest 4.1.11, `vi.resetModules()` resets modules but skips every id that starts with `mock:` (resetModules in vitest/dist/chunks/utils). The factory-mocked @sentry/nextjs from web/vitest.setup.ts, and its two vi.fn()s, therefore survive between cases, and web/vitest.config.ts sets no clearMocks. From the second reportError case on, `captured()` still holds the earlier calls. The exact toEqual checks fail, `const [[sent]] = captured()` reads the first case's error, and the noteError case's `expect(captured()).toEqual([])` fails too. Task 8 already clears these mocks in transport-storage.test.ts; doing the same here gives the isolation the comment assumes.
findings.suggested_fix: In report.test.ts's beforeEach, after re-importing the SDK, add `vi.mocked(sentry.captureException).mockClear(); vi.mocked(sentry.addBreadcrumb).mockClear();`. Reword the comment to say that resetModules re-evaluates report.ts but keeps the setup file's mocked SDK, which is why its calls are cleared here.
evidence: copy of it — and of the stand-in SDK from web/vitest.setup.ts, whose two mocks it calls.

findings.title: NotationSurface test's empty stand-in api crashes renderFinished case
findings.section: Task 14 — The music-font clock, and AlphaTab's own error event (Step 1, NotationSurface.test.tsx)
findings.why_it_matters: The case 'once a render has finished, hiding and showing the tab raises nothing a minute later' throws instead of passing. It calls the captured renderFinished handler, and that handler's last line, which the plan leaves unchanged, is `setRenderedTrackCount(api?.tracks.length ?? 0)` (NotationSurface.tsx:166). With STAND_IN_API = {}, the optional chain stops only at `api`, so `undefined.length` raises a TypeError inside act(). The same line also fails web's lint: unicorn/no-useless-undefined, with checkArguments on, is an error there. Its autofix, `?.()`, would not type-check against the `(args: unknown) => void` handler map. An empty `tracks` and a null argument fix both without changing what the case proves.
findings.suggested_fix: In Task 14 Step 1, declare `const STAND_IN_API: unknown = { tracks: [] };`, and say in its comment that the render handler reads `api.tracks`. Deliver the event as `act(() => handlers.get('renderFinished')?.(null));`.

findings.title: Several plan snippets fail web's lint and block their commits
findings.section: Tasks 2, 3, 5, 6 and 13 — code snippets (token check, known engine noise, report tests, envelope recorder, instruments tests)
findings.why_it_matters: These snippets fail web/eslint.config.mjs with errors that `eslint --fix` cannot repair, so each task's 'Lint, types, commit' step fails as written. That config also lints scripts/*.mjs, tests and e2e files, runs with --max-warnings 0, and lefthook's pre-commit runs `eslint --fix` on staged web files. (1) unicorn/no-array-callback-reference: `.flatMap(filesUnder)` in Task 2's script, `frames.every(isEngineFile)` in Task 3, and `bodies.flatMap(eventsIn)` in Task 6's recorder. (2) unicorn/consistent-function-scoping: the `stack` helper inside a describe (Task 3 test), `track` and `tagOn` (Task 5 test), `tagNow` inside the OpenFileControl case, and the `release` no-op initialisers (Task 13). (3) sonarjs/no-alphabetical-sort: the integrations case's bare `.toSorted()` (Task 6). I ran the repo's ESLint over the plan's exact code to confirm each one. Every fix is mechanical and changes no behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Edit the snippets. Wrap the passed functions in arrows: `.flatMap((dir) => filesUnder(dir))`, `.every((frame) => isEngineFile(frame))` and `.flatMap((body) => eventsIn(body))`. Move `stack`, `track`, `tagOn` and the OpenFileControl case's `tagNow` to module scope. Declare `let release!: (value: ArrayBuffer) => void;`, as player.e2e.ts:232 does for `releaseFont`. Sort with `.toSorted((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))`.
evidence: const track = (program: number) => ({ program, isPercussion: false });

findings.title: Home-page copy snippet carries a stray semicolon into JSX
findings.section: Task 7 — The three error pages, and the copy (Step 6, web/app/page.tsx)
findings.why_it_matters:
Pasted 'after the closing ' as instructed, the second fragment ends in `

;`. Inside JSX children that `;` is text, so the home page shows a stray ';' under the new privacy paragraph. Step 7 then regenerates landing-chromium-linux.png with the ';' in it, and no lint or type rule objects. The `;` and the `{ /* … */ }` block are what the repo's Prettier does to a tsx fence that opens with a JSX comment; running Prettier on such a fence reproduces both. Editing the fence alone will therefore not hold. Showing the whole new file, as Step 3 already does for the error pages, keeps the snippet valid JSX children.
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace Step 6's two fragments with the complete new `web/app/page.tsx`: its existing comments unchanged, the reworded tagline, and the new comment plus `

…

` after ``. Prettier then formats it as a component and adds no `;`.
